output.title: Decreasing Students' Stress Through Time Management Training

scenes.narration: Student mental health is a growing worldwide concern. Bayram and Bilgel asked how long minor signs of depression, anxiety, and stress should remain neglected.
scenes.layout_description: A student sits surrounded by large looming question marks and dark outline clouds.
scenes.visual_prompt: Hand-drawn black line art of a stressed university student at a desk, with minimal orange outline highlights on the surrounding floating question marks against a solid cream background.

scenes.narration: Pierceall and Keim found seventy-five percent of community college students perceived moderate stress, while thirteen percent reported high stress levels in their study.
scenes.layout_description: A simple hand-drawn pie chart highlights student stress percentages with bright orange and yellow accents.
scenes.visual_prompt: Black ink line art of a pie chart divided into sections, with a large 75% section filled in orange and a 13% section highlighted in yellow on an off-white background.

scenes.narration: Students often report unhealthy coping strategies for perceived stress, including drinking, smoking, and using illegal drugs, alongside risks of underachievement and dropout.
scenes.layout_description: Icons representing unhealthy coping mechanisms are grouped on the left, leading to an arrow pointing toward a dropout symbol on the right.
scenes.visual_prompt: Simple black line icons of a bottle, cigarette, and downward trending arrow, highlighted with orange circular line accents on a plain cream backdrop.

scenes.narration: Stress arises from social integration, exams, sleep changes, and financial concerns, but time-related demands like high workload and self-organized learning are severe problems.
scenes.layout_description: A central student figure is surrounded by small labeled boxes representing academic and temporal pressures.
scenes.visual_prompt: Hand-drawn figure of a student overwhelmed by stacked books and a clock, outlined in black ink with bright yellow accents on a cream background.

scenes.narration: Time management is recommended as a coping strategy to decrease stress. However, Van der Meer and colleagues described time management as a considerable concern.
scenes.layout_description: A calendar grid sits on the left with a large orange exclamation mark placed beside it on the right.
scenes.visual_prompt: Minimalist black line sketch of a wall calendar and a planner book, with a hand-lettered orange exclamation point on a solid cream background.

scenes.narration: Earlier research on time management interventions is scarce. Häfner and colleagues showed stress prevention, but no study had yet demonstrated a decrease in stress.
scenes.layout_description: A timeline shows past studies ending at a flat horizontal line marked with a question mark.
scenes.visual_prompt: Hand-drawn ink line timeline with published paper icons along it, featuring a yellow circle around a missing gap on a cream background.

scenes.narration: This study examined whether a time management training program could increase perceived control of time and decrease perceived stress across two post-training points.
scenes.layout_description: Two large arrows point in opposite directions, one going up and one going down.
scenes.visual_prompt: An upward arrow highlighted in yellow next to a downward arrow highlighted in orange, rendered in black hand-drawn line art on a cream background.

scenes.narration: Time management involves time assessment, goal setting, planning, and monitoring activities. Perceived control of time may act as a mediator to reduce perceived stress.
scenes.layout_description: Four sequential circular steps form a path leading from time management to reduced stress.
scenes.visual_prompt: A four-step linear flowchart drawn in black ink lines, with yellow circular step highlights on a clean off-white background.

scenes.narration: Correlational studies report mixed results. Bond and Feather found correlations with hopelessness, but Macan found non-significant correlations with job-induced or somatic tension.
scenes.layout_description: A balance scale shows conflicting research findings weighted on opposite sides.
scenes.visual_prompt: Simple hand-drawn line art scale balancing two piles of paper labeled with black ink, highlighted with orange accents on a cream background.

scenes.narration: In occupational settings, Macan found no effect of training, whereas Van Eerde reported positive effects on worry and Häfner and Stock reduced work stress.
scenes.layout_description: A office building outline contains symbols representing different study outcomes.
scenes.visual_prompt: Minimalist line drawing of an office building with small checkmarks and crosses drawn in black line and orange highlights on a solid cream background.

scenes.narration: The researchers hypothesized an increase in perceived control of time and a decrease in perceived stress, while self-reported demands would remain unchanged after training.
scenes.layout_description: Three horizontal bars display target trajectories: rising, falling, and remaining flat.
scenes.visual_prompt: Hand-drawn line graph showing three colored trend lines with orange and yellow highlights on a plain off-white background.

scenes.narration: The study utilized a non-equivalent dependent variable design. Training one group allows researchers to attribute changes specifically to the intervention if control variables stay stable.
scenes.layout_description: A single group box branches into measured outcome variables and an uninfluenced control variable.
scenes.visual_prompt: Black line diagram showing one participant box splitting into three outcome boxes, with an orange circle around the control variable on a cream background.

scenes.narration: Citing Frese and colleagues, this evaluation design effectively rules out testing, history, and placebo effects because both experimental and control variables are tested together.
scenes.layout_description: A shield motif sits over three crossed-out threat icons representing placebo, history, and testing effects.
scenes.visual_prompt: Hand-drawn black ink shield icon with orange highlight lines overlaying small crossed-out icons on a cream background.

scenes.narration: Perceived stress was measured using the tension scale. Perceived control of time was assessed, and external duties were measured as the control variable demands.
scenes.layout_description: Three clipboard icons represent the three primary constructs measured in the study.
scenes.visual_prompt: Three hand-drawn clipboards side-by-side in black line art, with orange and yellow corner highlights on a solid off-white backdrop.

scenes.narration: Twenty-three undergraduate students completed the four-hour training program. The intervention program covered prioritizing, goal setting, strategy development, daily planning, and monitoring ongoing study progress.
scenes.layout_description: A clock showing four hours sits next to a group silhouette of students.
scenes.visual_prompt: Minimalist sketch of a clock face highlighting four hours in yellow, next to a group of student outlines in black ink on a cream background.

scenes.narration: Participants reflected on activities, set concrete proximal goals, planned daily schedules with implementation intentions, and monitored completed tasks to evaluate their ongoing daily progress.
scenes.layout_description: A hand writes on a daily schedule checklist with checked task boxes.
scenes.visual_prompt: Hand-drawn close-up of a pencil filling in checkboxes on a daily schedule planner, with yellow highlight circles on checked boxes on a cream background.

scenes.narration: The final sample consisted of twenty-three German undergraduates with a mean age of twenty-three point thirty years, and about half were female.
scenes.layout_description: A simple demographic summary visual displaying student figures and key sample metrics.
scenes.visual_prompt: Line drawings of student figures with small text labels and an orange highlight circle around the sample count on a solid cream background.

scenes.narration: Before the intervention, about sixty percent of the students reported having no experience or little experience concerning the use of time management strategies.
scenes.layout_description: A simple bar chart shows baseline experience levels among the participants.
scenes.visual_prompt: Hand-drawn bar chart in black line art showing low baseline experience bars filled with yellow highlight ink on a cream background.

scenes.narration: Questionnaires were administered directly before training, two weeks after, and four weeks after training, ensuring all measurements occurred within the same ongoing semester.
scenes.layout_description: A linear calendar timeline highlights three distinct measurement points within one semester.
scenes.visual_prompt: Black line timeline with three distinct node points highlighted in bright orange along a horizontal path on an off-white background.

scenes.narration: Trainees reported a significant increase in strategy use four weeks after training, and a nearly significant increase two weeks after training, showing transfer.
scenes.layout_description: A tool icon moving from a classroom setting to a desk setting indicates skill transfer.
scenes.visual_prompt: Hand-drawn line sketch showing a gear icon moving from a group table to an individual desk, accented with orange arrows on a cream background.

scenes.narration: Two weeks after training, a repeated-measurement MANOVA revealed a significant overall time effect and a significant decrease in perceived stress, with a tendency toward control.
scenes.layout_description: A down arrow highlights the reduced stress score at the two-week mark.
scenes.visual_prompt: Line graph showing a dropping curve at week two, highlighted with an orange down arrow on a cream background.

scenes.narration: Four weeks after training, participants reported a significant decrease in perceived stress and a significant increase in perceived control of time compared to baseline.
scenes.layout_description: Two prominent trend lines show stress decreasing and control of time increasing at week four.
scenes.visual_prompt: Hand-drawn dual trend lines with yellow and orange highlight points at week four on a clean off-white background.

scenes.narration: Self-reported demands showed no significant changes two weeks or four weeks after training. This stability rules out major threats like testing or placebo effects.
scenes.layout_description: A perfectly flat line represents unchanged demands across all three time points.
scenes.visual_prompt: Horizontal flat line rendered in black line art across three points, framed by a yellow oval highlight on a cream background.

scenes.narration: Trainees with no or little experience benefited more than those with moderate experience, showing effect sizes more than twice as strong for stress reduction.
scenes.layout_description: A comparison visual contrasts high gains for beginners against modest gains for experienced students.
scenes.visual_prompt: Two vertical bar comparisons drawn in black ink, with the beginner group bar highlighted strongly in bright orange on a cream background.

scenes.narration: Prioritizing and daily planning may clarify study goals and lower effort, while daily monitoring provides reinforcing information about completed tasks to foster control.
scenes.layout_description: An open planner shows clear priorities leading to a calm student figure.
scenes.visual_prompt: Line drawing of a organized open desk planner with yellow highlight stars next to completed tasks on a cream background.

scenes.narration: Limitations include a small sample size of twenty-three students and a fifty percent dropout rate, meaning this study should be viewed as preliminary.
scenes.layout_description: A small group icon sits next to an outline of a larger drop-out group.
scenes.visual_prompt: Minimalist black line drawing of student figures with about half fading into light dashed lines, highlighted with an orange warning icon on a cream background.

scenes.narration: Time management training can lower student stress. Universities could offer short interventions, though larger studies comparing other stress interventions are needed for robust conclusions.
scenes.layout_description: A university building outline stands beside a clock and a supportive star icon.
scenes.visual_prompt: Hand-drawn line sketch of a university hall entrance with an orange star highlight and a yellow clock icon on a plain off-white background.
